description: Fact-checked chess quotes and trivia. Each entry was independently researched and sourced by an AI research agent using live web search, with instructions to exclude any claim it could not trace to a real, checkable source (book, interview, tournament record, or reputable chess-history reference such as chessgames.com or Edward Winter's chesshistory.com). Chess quote culture in particular is rife with misattribution, so unsourced or Edward-Winter-debunked quotes were deliberately excluded rather than included with a caveat.
model: Claude Sonnet 5 (research agents using live web search)

quotes.quote: I am more strongly confirmed than ever in the belief that the time devoted to chess is literally frittered away.
quotes.author: Paul Morphy
quotes.author_role: American chess prodigy, unofficial World Chess Champion 1858-1862
quotes.source: Letter to Daniel Willard Fiske, 4 February 1863

quotes.quote: Chess never has been and never can be aught but a recreation.
quotes.author: Paul Morphy
quotes.author_role: American chess prodigy, unofficial World Chess Champion 1858-1862
quotes.source: Speech, 'Testimonials to Paul Morphy,' University Hall, Boston, 25 May 1859

quotes.quote: It is not only the most delightful and scientific, but the most moral of amusements.
quotes.author: Paul Morphy
quotes.author_role: American chess prodigy, unofficial World Chess Champion 1858-1862
quotes.source: Speech, 'Testimonials to Paul Morphy,' Boston, 1859

quotes.quote: It is eminently and emphatically the philosopher's game.
quotes.author: Paul Morphy
quotes.author_role: American chess prodigy, unofficial World Chess Champion 1858-1862
quotes.source: Speech, 'Testimonials to Paul Morphy,' Boston, 1859

quotes.quote: Let the chessboard supersede the card-table, and a great improvement will be visible in the morals of the community.
quotes.author: Paul Morphy
quotes.author_role: American chess prodigy, unofficial World Chess Champion 1858-1862
quotes.source: Speech, 'Testimonials to Paul Morphy,' Boston, 1859

quotes.quote: It was Paul Morphy and his exploits that first induced me to enter chess life and to him I owe my career in the first instance.
quotes.author: Wilhelm Steinitz
quotes.source: International Chess Magazine, May 1886, p. 114

quotes.quote: As is well known, I, in common with most connoisseurs, hold that general contests only furnish a very unreliable and much inferior test of strength in comparison to matches between two selected players.
quotes.author: Wilhelm Steinitz
quotes.source: International Chess Magazine, June 1886, p. 170

quotes.quote: Life has often been compared with a game of chess, and no doubt the comparison fits in many respects.
quotes.author: Wilhelm Steinitz
quotes.source: Speech, New York, 16 October 1897, published in British Chess Magazine, December 1897, p. 471

quotes.quote: Of my opponent I am oblivious. For all that I know or note, he might as well be an abstraction or an automaton.
quotes.author: Wilhelm Steinitz
quotes.source: British Chess Magazine, September 1894, p. 366

quotes.quote: Good nature is the first element of a really strong intellect, and there is no really sound human brain without a sound sympathetic heart.
quotes.author: Wilhelm Steinitz
quotes.source: Speech, New York, 16 October 1897, published in British Chess Magazine, December 1897, p. 471

quotes.quote: On the chessboard, lies and hypocrisy do not survive long. The creative combination lays bare the presumption of a lie; the merciless fact, culminating in the checkmate, contradicts the hypocrite.
quotes.author: Emanuel Lasker
quotes.source: Lasker's Manual of Chess (1925 German ed.; 1932 English ed.)

quotes.quote: What is immobile must suffer violence. The light-winged bird will easily escape the huge dragon, but the firmly rooted big tree must remain where it is and may have to give up its leaves, fruit, perhaps its life.
quotes.author: Emanuel Lasker
quotes.source: Lasker's Manual of Chess (1925), p. 115

quotes.quote: You should keep in mind no names, nor numbers, nor isolated incidents, but only methods.
quotes.author: Emanuel Lasker
quotes.source: Lasker's Manual of Chess (1925), p. 338

quotes.quote: Of my fifty-seven years I have applied at least thirty to forgetting most of what I had learned or read, and since I succeeded in this I have acquired a certain ease and cheer which I should never again like to be without.
quotes.author: Emanuel Lasker
quotes.source: Lasker's Manual of Chess (1925), p. 337

quotes.quote: In order to improve your game you must study the endgame before anything else; for whereas the endings can be studied and mastered by themselves, the middle game and the opening must be studied in relation to the endgame.
quotes.author: José Raúl Capablanca
quotes.source: Chess Fundamentals (1921)

quotes.quote: A passed pawn increases in strength as the number of pieces on the board diminishes.
quotes.author: José Raúl Capablanca
quotes.source: Chess Fundamentals (1921)

quotes.quote: One must attempt to increase whatever weakness there may be in the opponent's position; or, if there is none, one or more must be created.
quotes.author: José Raúl Capablanca
quotes.source: Chess Fundamentals (1921)

quotes.quote: The fact that a player is very short of time is, to my mind, as little to be considered as an excuse as, for instance, the statement of the law-breaker that he was drunk at the moment he committed the crime.
quotes.author: Alexander Alekhine
quotes.source: Chess Life, Vol. 16-18 (1961), p. 113

quotes.quote: I study chess eight hours a day, on principle.
quotes.author: Alexander Alekhine
quotes.source: Quoted in David Hooper & Kenneth Whyld, The Oxford Companion to Chess (1996), p. 8

quotes.quote: Chess first of all teaches you to be objective.
quotes.author: Alexander Alekhine
quotes.source: Quoted in M. Yudovich & A. Kotov, The Soviet School of Chess (1958)

quotes.quote: Alekhine is a poet who creates a work of art out of something that would hardly inspire another man to send home a picture post card.
quotes.author: Max Euwe
quotes.source: Quoted in Fred Reinfeld, Why You Lose at Chess (1956), p. 180

quotes.quote: I honestly feel very humble when I study Capablanca's games.
quotes.author: Max Euwe
quotes.source: Quoted in David Hooper & Kenneth Whyld, The Oxford Companion to Chess (1996), p. 69

quotes.quote: First restrain, next blockade, lastly destroy.
quotes.author: Aron Nimzowitsch
quotes.author_role: Hypermodern chess theoretician, author of My System
quotes.source: My System (1925), p. 181

quotes.quote: The passed pawn is a criminal, who should be kept under lock and key. Mild measures such as police surveillance are not sufficient.
quotes.author: Aron Nimzowitsch
quotes.author_role: Hypermodern chess theoretician, author of My System
quotes.source: My System (1925), Chapter 4: 'The Passed Pawn'

quotes.quote: The threat is stronger than the execution.
quotes.author: Aron Nimzowitsch
quotes.author_role: Hypermodern chess theoretician, author of My System
quotes.source: Skakbladet, No. 9 (1933), p. 137

quotes.quote: The beauty of a move lies not in its appearance but in the thought behind it.
quotes.author: Aron Nimzowitsch
quotes.author_role: Hypermodern chess theoretician, author of My System
quotes.source: Quoted in Fred Reinfeld, Nimzovich: The Hypermodern (1948) — secondary source, exact original wording/context unverified

quotes.quote: Tempo is the soul of chess.
quotes.author: Siegbert Tarrasch
quotes.author_role: Leading chess theoretician and teacher, 'Praeceptor Germaniae'
quotes.source: Tarrasch's Schachzeitung, 15 November 1933, p. 56

quotes.quote: It is not enough to be a good player; one must play well.
quotes.author: Siegbert Tarrasch
quotes.author_role: Leading chess theoretician and teacher, 'Praeceptor Germaniae'
quotes.source: Chess Player's Chronicle, 20 September 1890, pp. 196-198

quotes.quote: Before the endgame, the gods have placed the middlegame.
quotes.author: Siegbert Tarrasch
quotes.author_role: Leading chess theoretician and teacher, 'Praeceptor Germaniae'
quotes.source: Annotation to Wolf v Tarrasch, Monte Carlo 1903, in Die moderne Schachpartie

quotes.quote: Chess, like love, like music, has the power to make men happy.
quotes.author: Siegbert Tarrasch
quotes.author_role: Leading chess theoretician and teacher, 'Praeceptor Germaniae'
quotes.source: Das Schachspiel (1931), p. 4; English ed. The Game of Chess (1935), p. xi

quotes.quote: When one sees a strong move, one must ask if there is not a stronger one.
quotes.author: Siegbert Tarrasch
quotes.author_role: Leading chess theoretician and teacher, 'Praeceptor Germaniae'
quotes.source: Das Schachspiel (1931), p. 164; English ed. The Game of Chess (1935), p. 122

quotes.quote: As long as an opening is reputed to be weak it can be tried.
quotes.author: Savielly Tartakower
quotes.source: My Best Games of Chess, 1905-1930, Vol. I (1953), p. 17

quotes.quote: You really have confidence in your pieces.
quotes.author: Savielly Tartakower
quotes.source: Remark to Siegbert Tarrasch, Semmering 1926, quoted in My Best Games of Chess, Vol. I (1953), p. 157

quotes.quote: The art of chess is simple: you play Kt-B3-K5 and then, sooner or later, KtxKBP is decisive.
quotes.author: Savielly Tartakower
quotes.source: My Best Games of Chess, Vol. II (1956), p. 61

quotes.quote: It is only a strong player who knows how weakly he plays.
quotes.author: Savielly Tartakower
quotes.source: Chess Pie (1922), p. 28

quotes.quote: An isolated pawn spreads gloom over the whole board.
quotes.author: Savielly Tartakower
quotes.source: Schachmethodik, 2nd edition (Berlin, 1929), p. 113

quotes.quote: Of good moves have no fear.
quotes.author: Savielly Tartakower
quotes.source: Deutsche Schachzeitung, December 1927, p. 354

quotes.quote: The mistakes are all there, waiting to be made.
quotes.author: Savielly Tartakower
quotes.source: Die Hypermoderne Schachpartie (Vienna, 1924), p. 90

quotes.quote: Chess is a fighting game which is purely intellectual and excludes chance.
quotes.author: Richard Réti
quotes.source: Modern Ideas in Chess (London, 1923), p. 104

quotes.quote: Those chess lovers who ask me how many moves I calculate in advance, when making a combination, are always astonished when I reply, quite truthfully, 'as a rule not a single one.'
quotes.author: Richard Réti
quotes.source: Modern Ideas in Chess (1923)

quotes.quote: Lasker often deliberately plays badly.
quotes.author: Richard Réti
quotes.source: Masters of the Chess Board (1933) — a claim Lasker himself strongly objected to in a 1936 letter

quotes.quote: Capablanca's calm style, the harmonic combination of very exact positional understanding with a calculation of variations, imparted a particular elegance to the Cuban's games.
quotes.author: Mikhail Botvinnik
quotes.source: Achieving the Aim (Pergamon Press, 1981), p. 90

quotes.quote: As a player Keres had failings which were well known to me. The first was his slight uncertainty when he had to orientate himself in new opening schemes.
quotes.author: Mikhail Botvinnik
quotes.source: Achieving the Aim (Pergamon Press, 1981), p. 110

quotes.quote: It is clear now to many people that Fischer has a maniacal fear of beginning a competition.
quotes.author: Mikhail Botvinnik
quotes.source: Achieving the Aim (Pergamon Press, 1981), p. 198

quotes.quote: A Jew by blood, a Russian by culture, Soviet by upbringing.
quotes.author: Mikhail Botvinnik
quotes.source: Achieving the Aim (Pergamon Press, 1981), p. 178

quotes.quote: When the game takes on a more or less open character, and when piece-play is important, nobody can equal Tal... In other positions he is weaker. Here no calculation can help him.
quotes.author: Mikhail Botvinnik
quotes.source: Chess Life magazine, June 1962, p. 135

quotes.quote: I think Capablanca had the greatest natural talent. When a great pianist plays, we don't hear separate notes, but we hear a musical picture. So too, Capablanca didn't make separate moves - he was creating a chess picture. Nobody could compare with him in this.
quotes.author: Mikhail Botvinnik
quotes.source: Chess Life magazine, March 1984

quotes.quote: When my opponent's clock is going I discuss general considerations in an internal dialogue with myself. When my own clock is going I analyse concrete variations.
quotes.author: Mikhail Botvinnik
quotes.source: Quoted in Think Like a Grandmaster by Alexander Kotov (London, 1971), p. 139

quotes.quote: The world champions die in the strict order of their succession to the title. Thus the writer of these lines is the next on the list.
quotes.author: Mikhail Botvinnik
quotes.source: Europe Echecs, April 1983, p. 13

quotes.quote: I had still tried not to lose the sense of humour that is so essential both for the struggle and for victory in this field.
quotes.author: Mikhail Botvinnik
quotes.source: Statement dated 3 May 1957, quoted in The World Chess Championship 1957 by Harry Golombek, p. 139

quotes.quote: When an electronic machine has started playing chess and played it successfully this will be such a momentous event that every schoolboy will want to know about it.
quotes.author: Mikhail Botvinnik
quotes.source: Chess magazine, October 1968, p. 8

quotes.quote: In my opinion, the style of a player should not be formed under the influence of any single great master.
quotes.author: Vasily Smyslov
quotes.source: 125 Selected Games (Pergamon/Oxford, 1983), p. 4 - English edition of V poiskakh garmonii (In Search of Harmony), 1979

quotes.quote: In chess I am also a staunch supporter of classical clarity of thought. The content of a game should be a search for truth, and victory a demonstration of its rightness.
quotes.author: Vasily Smyslov
quotes.source: 125 Selected Games (Pergamon/Oxford, 1983), p. 5

quotes.quote: No fantasy, however rich, no technique, however masterly, no penetration into the psychology of the opponent, however deep, can make a chess game a work of art if these qualities do not lead to the main goal - the search for truth.
quotes.author: Vasily Smyslov
quotes.source: 125 Selected Games (Pergamon/Oxford, 1983), p. 5

quotes.quote: My study of chess was accompanied by a strong attraction to music, and it was probably thanks to this that from childhood I became accustomed to thinking of chess as an art, and have never regarded it as anything else, for all the science and sport involved in it.
quotes.author: Vasily Smyslov
quotes.source: 125 Selected Games (Pergamon/Oxford, 1983)

quotes.quote: Such a 'mutual understanding' with the pieces enables a player to see that which often remains concealed to purely logical analysis. It is then that the innate ability of a player, which I call a sense of harmony, manifests itself.
quotes.author: Vasily Smyslov
quotes.source: 125 Selected Games (Pergamon/Oxford, 1983)

quotes.quote: Talent in chess... I think it's the feeling of harmony. How quickly the player understands the position, how well is their intuition developed.
quotes.author: Vasily Smyslov
quotes.source: 75th-birthday interview with Yakov Damsky, 1996

quotes.quote: not a work of reference but a book kept under my pillow - a bedtime story for a chess child
quotes.author: Tigran Petrosian
quotes.source: On Aron Nimzowitsch's My System, quoted in The Games of Tigran Petrosian, Volume I, ed. Eduard Shekhtman (Pergamon, 1991)

quotes.quote: the teaching of positional play is equivalent to the teaching of chess in general
quotes.author: Tigran Petrosian
quotes.source: The Games of Tigran Petrosian, Volume I, ed. Eduard Shekhtman (Pergamon, 1991)

quotes.quote: Botvinnik, like no-one else, is able to arrive for the start of an event in the highest state of preparedness and from the very first moves to play at full strength.
quotes.author: Tigran Petrosian
quotes.source: On the 1963 World Championship match, in The Games of Tigran Petrosian, Volume I, ed. Eduard Shekhtman (Pergamon, 1991)

quotes.quote: Looking back, I rarely recall vexations and disappointments. Compared with the joys which chess has generously given me, they are mere trifles.
quotes.author: Tigran Petrosian
quotes.source: The Games of Tigran Petrosian, Volume I, ed. Eduard Shekhtman (Pergamon, 1991), p. 216

quotes.quote: I began seriously wondering whether I shouldn't give up chess.
quotes.author: Tigran Petrosian
quotes.source: On being passed over for the 1956 Amsterdam Candidates delegation, in The Games of Tigran Petrosian, Volume I, ed. Eduard Shekhtman (Pergamon, 1991), pp. 215-216

quotes.quote: When I knew that, I was down on the stage, instead of up here.
quotes.author: Tigran Petrosian
quotes.source: Self-deprecating reply to a spectator's question during a public post-mortem; quoted in Anatoly Karpov: Chess is My Life by Karpov and Roshal (Pergamon/Oxford, 1980), p. 166

quotes.quote: I have a weakness for any piece in excess of my opponent's numbers - from pawn to queen.
quotes.author: Tigran Petrosian
quotes.source: Vik L. Vasilev, Tigran Petrosian: His Life and Games (Batsford, London, 1974), p. 166

quotes.quote: I have no further ambitions for the world's championship.
quotes.author: Boris Spassky
quotes.source: Reported account from the Winnipeg international grandmaster tournament, 1967 (per Edward Winter, chesshistory.com)

quotes.quote: Personally, I think the best chessplayer of all time was Capablanca - especially because he was very lazy, and I am lazy too. So I can understand him very easily. But he was a real genius.
quotes.author: Boris Spassky
quotes.source: Chess Life magazine, April 1983, pp. 12-13

quotes.quote: Probably there have been two pure geniuses in chess; Morphy and Capablanca.
quotes.author: Boris Spassky
quotes.source: Interview with Leonard Barden, Chess Life & Review, January 1970

quotes.quote: Only when Mikhail Tal appeared did chessplayers see that there could be a different style.
quotes.author: Boris Spassky
quotes.source: Interview with Leonard Barden, Chess Life & Review, January 1970

quotes.quote: I love chess, but I hate it as a profession. You must kill your opponent. I just want to reflect myself on the board.
quotes.author: Boris Spassky
quotes.source: Interview with Grant Segall, Sun-Sentinel (Florida), August 8, 1985

quotes.quote: I call him 'Hand' because his hand knows exactly on which square to put which piece.
quotes.author: Boris Spassky
quotes.source: On Vasily Smyslov, quoted in Kingpin magazine, Autumn 1998, p. 23

quotes.quote: Overall, of course, I knew the openings badly, but in my own systems I felt confident.
quotes.author: Boris Spassky
quotes.source: Interview with Soviet Sport, translated and published at chessintranslation.com, January 2012 (interview conducted 2010)

quotes.quote: When you play Bobby, it is not a question of whether you win or lose. It is a question of whether you survive.
quotes.author: Boris Spassky
quotes.source: Quoted as epigraph in Bobby Fischer Goes to War by David Edmonds and John Eidinow (2004)

quotes.quote: I always want to be first. If I weren't a chessplayer, all the same I would aim to be first at something.
quotes.author: Anatoly Karpov
quotes.source: 1976 interview with foreign journalists, quoted in Anatoly Karpov: Chess is My Life (Karpov and Roshal, Pergamon/Oxford, 1980)

quotes.quote: In general one has to learn not to lose, and wins will then come of their own accord.
quotes.author: Anatoly Karpov
quotes.source: Anatoly Karpov: Chess is My Life (Karpov and Roshal, Pergamon/Oxford, 1980), p. 59

quotes.quote: The rapidity of my play is not at all, as some think, due to the fact that everything is clear to me. Simply I don't wish to get into time trouble.
quotes.author: Anatoly Karpov
quotes.source: Anatoly Karpov: Chess is My Life (Karpov and Roshal, Pergamon/Oxford, 1980), p. 59

quotes.quote: Sacrifice a piece? Why not sacrifice if, of course, it is correct. Only I do not intend to burn my boats, as some do.
quotes.author: Anatoly Karpov
quotes.source: Anatoly Karpov: Chess is My Life (Karpov and Roshal, Pergamon/Oxford, 1980), p. 59

quotes.quote: If you don't believe in victory you have no business sitting down to a chess board.
quotes.author: Anatoly Karpov
quotes.source: The Batsford Chess Yearbook by Kevin J. O'Connell (London, 1975), p. 16; also in 64 magazine, issue 48, 29 Nov-5 Dec 1974, p. 10

quotes.quote: We were only testing the equipment.
quotes.author: Anatoly Karpov
quotes.source: On the colorless 18-move draw in game one of the 1978 World Championship match, quoted in Chess Scandals: The 1978 World Chess Championship by Edward B. Edmondson and Mikhail Tal (Pergamon, 1981)

quotes.quote: I myself have been travelling around the world for 20 years, and I have never met a chessplayer who would agree to join me for a visit to an art gallery.
quotes.author: Anatoly Karpov
quotes.source: Karpov on Karpov: Memoirs of a Chess World Champion, trans. Todd Bludeau (Atheneum, 1990)

quotes.quote: I don't know anyone else in the history of chess to whom we owe so much... No-one from our generation of chessplayers, nor the one to follow, should ever forget that we are living off the dividends guaranteed us by Robert James Fischer.
quotes.author: Anatoly Karpov
quotes.source: Karpov on Karpov: Memoirs of a Chess World Champion, trans. Todd Bludeau (Atheneum, 1990)

quotes.quote: Every match is preceded by scandalous situations. Some arise spontaneously, others are planned, but in general a match never comes off without them.
quotes.author: Anatoly Karpov
quotes.source: Karpov on Karpov: Memoirs of a Chess World Champion, trans. Todd Bludeau (Atheneum, 1990)

quotes.quote: Later, I began to succeed in decisive games, perhaps because I realised a very simple truth: not only was I worried, but so was my opponent.
quotes.author: Mikhail Tal
quotes.source: The Life and Games of Mikhail Tal (Cadogan/RHM, first English ed. 1976)

quotes.quote: To play for a draw, at any rate with White, is to some degree a crime against chess.
quotes.author: Mikhail Tal
quotes.source: The Life and Games of Mikhail Tal (Cadogan/RHM, first English ed. 1976)

quotes.quote: I do not like annotating other people's games... it is very difficult to penetrate into a player's thinking.
quotes.author: Mikhail Tal
quotes.source: The Life and Games of Mikhail Tal (New York, 1976), p. 25

quotes.quote: I spent 15 minutes looking at the position before I saw it, and my opponent didn't see it at all.
quotes.author: Mikhail Tal
quotes.source: On a puzzle from his own 1973 game against Platonov; quoted by William Hartston in Now! magazine, 4-10 January 1980, p. 98

quotes.quote: Chess are leisure... also a science... also a sport. But are chess only a sport?
quotes.author: Mikhail Tal
quotes.source: Television interview, Ostankino, 1987

quotes.quote: I prefer not to study chess but to play it. For me chess is more an art than a science.
quotes.author: Mikhail Tal
quotes.source: Television interview, Ostankino, 1987

quotes.quote: The secret of the game's attraction is its beauty and logic; the secret of its eternal youth is its variety and inexhaustibility; the secret of mastering it is knowledge and experience.
quotes.author: Mikhail Tal
quotes.source: Tal's Winning Chess Combinations (RHM Press, 1979)

quotes.quote: In my opinion, the King's Gambit is busted. It loses by force.
quotes.author: Bobby Fischer
quotes.source: Essay "A Bust to the King's Gambit," American Chess Quarterly, Vol. 1, No. 1

quotes.quote: Tactics flow from a positionally superior game.
quotes.author: Bobby Fischer
quotes.source: My 60 Memorable Games (book, annotation on the Sherwin vs. Fischer game)

quotes.quote: Best by test.
quotes.author: Bobby Fischer
quotes.source: My 60 Memorable Games (book, remark on 1.e4)

quotes.quote: I am the best player in the world, and I am here to prove it.
quotes.author: Bobby Fischer
quotes.source: Chess Digest Magazine, Vol. 4, p. 263

quotes.quote: I'm not afraid of him, he's afraid of me.
quotes.author: Bobby Fischer
quotes.source: Interview prior to the 1972 World Championship match against Spassky

quotes.quote: I object to being called a chess genius because I consider myself to be an all around genius who just happens to play chess, which is rather different.
quotes.author: Bobby Fischer
quotes.source: Radio interview

quotes.quote: I think once you start distrusting your own mind you're finished.
quotes.author: Bobby Fischer
quotes.source: Interview, Ambassador Report magazine

quotes.quote: I don't believe in psychology. I believe in good moves.
quotes.author: Bobby Fischer
quotes.source: Interview with The Washington Post, on the eve of the 1972 Spassky match, responding to a question about being "on edge"

quotes.quote: Capablanca was possibly the greatest player in the entire history of chess.
quotes.author: Bobby Fischer
quotes.source: Interview during the 1960 Chess Olympiad, published in Ajedrez Español

quotes.quote: [Lasker was] a coffee-house player who knew nothing about openings and didn't understand positional chess.
quotes.author: Bobby Fischer
quotes.source: "The Ten Greatest Masters in History," Chessworld magazine

quotes.quote: Many consider Alekhine a great opening theoretician, but I don't think he was.
quotes.author: Bobby Fischer
quotes.source: Chessworld magazine, January-February issue

quotes.quote: Paul Morphy was a great chessplayer, a genius.
quotes.author: Bobby Fischer
quotes.source: Press conference

quotes.quote: Botvinnik and Tal are among the best; I also like Spassky, but I think Petrosian is better than all of them.
quotes.author: Bobby Fischer
quotes.source: Interview at the 1960 Chess Olympiad

quotes.quote: There's no comparison. Now there are far more good players, and technical knowledge is more extensive.
quotes.author: Bobby Fischer
quotes.source: Interview at the 1960 Chess Olympiad, on how the chess world had changed

quotes.quote: The public must come to see that chess is a violent sport. Chess is mental torture.
quotes.author: Garry Kasparov
quotes.source: Quoted in Martin Amis's review of "Kasparov-Short" by Raymond Keene, Independent on Sunday

quotes.quote: It's not enough to be talented. It's not enough to work hard and to study late into the night. You must also become intimately aware of the methods you use to reach your decisions.
quotes.author: Garry Kasparov
quotes.source: How Life Imitates Chess, Part I Chapter 1 "The Lesson," p. 14

quotes.quote: Having spent a lifetime analyzing the game of chess and comparing the capacity of computers to the capacity of the human brain, I've often wondered, where does our success come from? The answer is synthesis, the ability to combine creativity and calculation, art and science, into a whole that is much greater than the sum of its parts.
quotes.author: Garry Kasparov
quotes.source: How Life Imitates Chess, Opening Gambit section "Why Chess?," p. 4

quotes.quote: With each success the ability to change is reduced. My longtime friend and coach Grandmaster Yuri Dokhoian, aptly compared it to being dipped in bronze. Each victory added another coat.
quotes.author: Garry Kasparov
quotes.source: How Life Imitates Chess, Part I Chapter 2 "Strategy," p. 34

quotes.quote: This obligation to move can be a burden to a player without strategic vision.
quotes.author: Garry Kasparov
quotes.source: How Life Imitates Chess, Part I Chapter 3 "Strategy And Tactics At Work," p. 36

quotes.quote: You must also have a sense of when to stop.
quotes.author: Garry Kasparov
quotes.source: How Life Imitates Chess, Part I Chapter 4 "Calculation," p. 51

quotes.quote: I like to say that the attacker always has the advantage.
quotes.author: Garry Kasparov
quotes.source: How Life Imitates Chess, Part II Chapter 10 "The Attacker's Advantage," p. 122

quotes.quote: If you're already in a fight, you want the first blow to be the last and you had better be the one to throw it.
quotes.author: Garry Kasparov
quotes.source: How Life Imitates Chess, Part II Chapter 10 "The Attacker's Advantage," p. 130

quotes.quote: Question the status quo at all times, especially when things are going well.
quotes.author: Garry Kasparov
quotes.source: How Life Imitates Chess, Part III Chapter 11 "Question Success," p. 135

quotes.quote: In chess, bigamy is acceptable but monarchy is absolute.
quotes.author: Garry Kasparov
quotes.source: How Life Imitates Chess, Part II Chapter 8 "Exchanges And Imbalances," p. 102

quotes.quote: Deep Blue was as intelligent as your alarm clock.
quotes.author: Garry Kasparov
quotes.source: Interview, "Kasparov On Facing Deep Blue: 'I Was Part Of Something Really Unique'", Chess.com

quotes.quote: I feel I was beaten by IBM, not by Deep Blue.
quotes.author: Garry Kasparov
quotes.source: The Garry Kasparov Interview, Part 1, ChessBase

quotes.quote: It was a sad day for chess. Scientifically speaking, the match was a fake.
quotes.author: Garry Kasparov
quotes.source: The Garry Kasparov Interview, Part 1, ChessBase, on the 1997 Deep Blue rematch

quotes.quote: What is success? Winning occasionally isn't the thing, it's about being on top for twenty years.
quotes.author: Garry Kasparov
quotes.source: The Garry Kasparov Interview, Part 1, ChessBase

quotes.quote: The Kasparov-Karpov matches were the foundations of modern chess.
quotes.author: Garry Kasparov
quotes.source: The Garry Kasparov Interview, Part 1, ChessBase

quotes.quote: There's no more room for bluffs. Technology changed our ability to prepare for the game.
quotes.author: Garry Kasparov
quotes.source: Interview, "There's no more room for bluffs," The Talks

quotes.quote: The difference between a chess engine that you can buy and install your computer, and Magnus Carlsen...is about the same as the difference between Usain Bolt and a Ferrari.
quotes.author: Garry Kasparov
quotes.source: Interview, The Talks

quotes.quote: We should look for humans working with machines rather than fighting them.
quotes.author: Garry Kasparov
quotes.source: Interview, The Talks

quotes.quote: The human mind isn't a computer; it cannot progress in an orderly fashion down a list of candidate moves and rank them by a score down to the hundredth of a pawn the way a chess machine does.
quotes.author: Garry Kasparov
quotes.source: Deep Thinking: Where Machine Intelligence Ends and Human Creativity Begins (book)

quotes.quote: My nature is that I have to excite myself with a big challenge.
quotes.author: Garry Kasparov
quotes.source: Guardian interview by Stephen Moss, "Why Kasparov Quit Chess"

quotes.quote: As a chess player, I know that strategy is the future impact of present decisions. However grand our plans are for two, five, even ten moves ahead, it's the move that we make now that determines that future.
quotes.author: Garry Kasparov
quotes.source: TED talk, "Stand with Ukraine in the fight against evil"

quotes.quote: In chess, we say that the player with the initiative is obliged to attack, otherwise the initiative will be lost and the counterattack will likely be decisive.
quotes.author: Garry Kasparov
quotes.source: "The Truth About Putin," The Weekly Standard

quotes.quote: This turned out to be a terrible blunder, the worst of my career.
quotes.author: Garry Kasparov
quotes.source: Garry Kasparov on My Great Predecessors (book), on breaking away to found the rival PCA in 1993, Heinemann edition p. 115

quotes.quote: I was late to adopt computers into my training regime. At the beginning of my career I used computers only for their game databases.
quotes.author: Vladimir Kramnik
quotes.source: "Vladimir Kramnik on Man vs Machine," ChessBase

quotes.quote: It was already difficult, but still not totally impossible, for a human to beat a top computer program. But within maybe after two or three years it became completely impossible.
quotes.author: Vladimir Kramnik
quotes.source: "Vladimir Kramnik on Man vs Machine," ChessBase

quotes.quote: Computers may now be stronger than the human World Champion, but this achievement does not change the real value of the game: the pleasure that we humans get from playing one another.
quotes.author: Vladimir Kramnik
quotes.source: "Vladimir Kramnik on Man vs Machine," ChessBase

quotes.quote: I'm absolutely convinced that Garry was still a much stronger player than Deep Blue.
quotes.author: Vladimir Kramnik
quotes.source: "Vladimir Kramnik on Man vs Machine," ChessBase

quotes.quote: Well… it's not bad for chess, it's just bad for chess players.
quotes.author: Vladimir Kramnik
quotes.source: "Kramnik on health, plans – and computers," ChessBase

quotes.quote: My own play is not based on calculation, so that in spite of all the plusses which computers have I also have a few trumps myself.
quotes.author: Vladimir Kramnik
quotes.source: "Kramnik on health, plans – and computers," ChessBase

quotes.quote: Computers have changed the world of chess. That is pretty clear.
quotes.author: Vladimir Kramnik
quotes.source: "Kramnik on health, plans – and computers," ChessBase

quotes.quote: For most players, winning is by far the main goal. But since my childhood, I have not been competitive at all.
quotes.author: Vladimir Kramnik
quotes.source: "Vladimir Kramnik Interview: 'I'm Not Afraid To Lose'", Chess.com

quotes.quote: I was never intimidated or felt afraid of anyone. I think this particularly helped against Garry, whenever we played.
quotes.author: Vladimir Kramnik
quotes.source: "Vladimir Kramnik Interview: 'I'm Not Afraid To Lose'", Chess.com

quotes.quote: If you don't get intimidated, nobody can intimidate you.
quotes.author: Vladimir Kramnik
quotes.source: "Vladimir Kramnik Interview: 'I'm Not Afraid To Lose'", Chess.com

quotes.quote: He rarely won tournaments but he was the best defensive player in the world without a doubt.
quotes.author: Vladimir Kramnik
quotes.source: "Vladimir Kramnik Interview: 'I'm Not Afraid To Lose'", Chess.com, on Peter Leko

quotes.quote: I always said that I will quit chess when I stop enjoying it.
quotes.author: Vladimir Kramnik
quotes.source: "Vladimir Kramnik Interview: 'I'm Not Afraid To Lose'", Chess.com

quotes.quote: There are no excuses. You always have to be the best.
quotes.author: Magnus Carlsen
quotes.source: CNN interview, quoted in ChessBase, May 29, 2020

quotes.quote: At a time when all players prepare themselves with software, my goal is not to see if my computer is better than my opponent's.
quotes.author: Magnus Carlsen
quotes.source: Le Monde interview, quoted in ChessBase ("Magnus Carlsen explains his approach to chess"), April 19, 2014

quotes.quote: In the openings, I just need to reach a position that gives me play. The idea is to be smart rather than trying to crush the other.
quotes.author: Magnus Carlsen
quotes.source: Le Monde interview, quoted in ChessBase ("Magnus Carlsen explains his approach to chess"), April 19, 2014

quotes.quote: I don't quite fit into the usual schemes.
quotes.author: Magnus Carlsen
quotes.source: ChessBase interview ("Magnus Carlsen – 'I don't quite fit into the usual schemes'"), December 22, 2011

quotes.quote: My fundamental chess understanding was formed without machine involvement.
quotes.author: Magnus Carlsen
quotes.source: ChessBase interview ("Magnus Carlsen – 'I don't quite fit into the usual schemes'"), December 22, 2011

quotes.quote: I've never been much of a computer guy at least in terms of playing with computers. Actually until I was about 11 I didn't use a computer for preparing for games at all. I was playing a bit online, was using the chess club mainly.
quotes.author: Magnus Carlsen
quotes.source: Business Insider interview by Gus Lubin, September 4, 2012

quotes.quote: Either you play as if it matters or you don't.
quotes.author: Viswanathan Anand
quotes.source: Chess.com interview ("Vishy Anand Interview: 'It comes as a shock that people suddenly see you as the veteran'"), May 14, 2020

quotes.quote: Some of the work that took us one or two weeks back in 1995 with a team of four people working full time, the computer finds in exactly two seconds.
quotes.author: Viswanathan Anand
quotes.source: Chess.com interview ("Vishy Anand Interview: 'It comes as a shock that people suddenly see you as the veteran'"), May 14, 2020

quotes.quote: But crucially my attitude and the technology were in sync. I was in the mood to take risks, and I was really eager to learn and do something new.
quotes.author: Viswanathan Anand
quotes.source: Chess.com interview ("Vishy Anand Interview: 'It comes as a shock that people suddenly see you as the veteran'"), May 14, 2020

quotes.quote: I particularly hated the fact that it happened in Chennai. Of all the matches I played, it had to be this one that I lose in my home town.
quotes.author: Viswanathan Anand
quotes.source: Chess.com interview ("Vishy Anand Interview: 'It comes as a shock that people suddenly see you as the veteran'"), May 14, 2020

quotes.quote: I had a dream probably around the age of 10 that I would become world champion.
quotes.author: Fabiano Caruana
quotes.author_role: World Chess Championship Challenger 2018; World No. 2
quotes.source: Chess.com interview ("Caruana: 'I Had A Dream I Would Become World Chess Champion'"), April 12, 2024

quotes.quote: It's not possible to say, 'Be more psychologically stable!' It's something that just happens in the moment and you can't prepare for it, you can't train for it.
quotes.author: Fabiano Caruana
quotes.author_role: World Chess Championship Challenger 2018; World No. 2
quotes.source: Chess.com interview ("Caruana: 'I Had A Dream I Would Become World Chess Champion'"), April 12, 2024

quotes.quote: He is the player who is overall the strongest, the most accurate, and the most consistent.
quotes.author: Fabiano Caruana
quotes.author_role: World Chess Championship Challenger 2018; World No. 2
quotes.source: Chess.com interview ("Fabiano Caruana On Playing A World Championship, On Carlsen-Nepomniachtchi, And More"), November 5, 2021

quotes.quote: The idea isn't to wipe your opponent off the board; the idea is to maximize your equity.
quotes.author: Fabiano Caruana
quotes.author_role: World Chess Championship Challenger 2018; World No. 2
quotes.source: Chess.com interview ("Fabiano Caruana On Playing A World Championship, On Carlsen-Nepomniachtchi, And More"), November 5, 2021

quotes.quote: I love chess, but if you're just obsessed with that one thing, eventually you will go a little bit insane.
quotes.author: Hikaru Nakamura
quotes.source: Chess.com interview ("Hikaru Nakamura Interview: Cause Of A Chess Boom?"), February 4, 2019

quotes.quote: In many ways, chess is better than the real world.
quotes.author: Hikaru Nakamura
quotes.source: Chess.com interview ("Hikaru Nakamura Interview: Cause Of A Chess Boom?"), February 4, 2019

quotes.quote: I'd like to be competitive until I'm 40, but beyond that I'd like to do something else.
quotes.author: Hikaru Nakamura
quotes.source: Chess.com interview ("Hikaru Nakamura Interview: Cause Of A Chess Boom?"), February 4, 2019

quotes.quote: I don't want to be that famous, to be written about every day, or interviewed after every tournament.
quotes.author: Ding Liren
quotes.source: Chess.com interview ("Ding Liren Interview: 'I Don't Want To Be Famous'"), February 2, 2020

quotes.quote: There is a price to fame. Of course I will earn more money if I become more well-known and maybe have better status, but I also won't have my own time.
quotes.author: Ding Liren
quotes.source: Chess.com interview ("Ding Liren Interview: 'I Don't Want To Be Famous'"), February 2, 2020

quotes.quote: A match is a match. It's between two players. When one player starts to hit his stride, how the opponent reacts depends on their experience and how they handle the situation at the moment.
quotes.author: Ding Liren
quotes.source: FIDE interview ("Ding Liren ahead of his World Championship showdown with Gukesh: 'A match is a match'"), 2024

quotes.quote: The only people who I truly dislike are those who buy and sell games, ratings and titles.
quotes.author: Ian Nepomniachtchi
quotes.source: Chess.com interview ("Ian Nepomniachtchi Interview: 'I Dislike Players Who Buy And Sell Games'"), October 28, 2019

quotes.quote: Of course I love chess. However, sometimes I'm envious of amateurs who can play and enjoy chess and not have to care about their results.
quotes.author: Ian Nepomniachtchi
quotes.source: Chess.com interview ("Ian Nepomniachtchi Interview: 'I Dislike Players Who Buy And Sell Games'"), October 28, 2019

quotes.quote: I think that everyone is different and peculiar. Strong players are not an exception, they all are unique and unlike each other.
quotes.author: Ian Nepomniachtchi
quotes.source: Chess.com interview ("Ian Nepomniachtchi Interview: 'I Dislike Players Who Buy And Sell Games'"), October 28, 2019

quotes.quote: Chess was a way out for me.
quotes.author: Wesley So
quotes.source: Chess.com interview ("Wesley So Interview: 'Chess Was A Way Out'"), April 10, 2019

quotes.quote: Chess is the poor man's game. Rich people play tennis, polo, and golf, while poor people play chess because you don't need anything.
quotes.author: Wesley So
quotes.source: Chess.com interview ("Wesley So Interview: 'Chess Was A Way Out'"), April 10, 2019

quotes.quote: I play best when I'm very happy. The times when I'm not happy, you can see it in my play.
quotes.author: Wesley So
quotes.source: Chess.com interview ("Wesley So Interview: 'Chess Was A Way Out'"), April 10, 2019

quotes.quote: Well, I never thought I would be number two. But now that I'm here, I want to try to be number one. I'm not entirely satisfied with number two.
quotes.author: Wesley So
quotes.source: Washington Post interview, quoted in ChessBase ("Wesley So: 'I'm not entirely satisfied with (world) number two'"), June 2017

quotes.quote: I don't believe in predictions and who are the favorites. I just think whoever shows up every day as the best will win the game eventually.
quotes.author: Gukesh Dommaraju
quotes.source: FIDE interview ("Gukesh Dommaraju: 'I just want to enjoy the experience'"), November 10, 2024

quotes.quote: I just want to enjoy the experience.
quotes.author: Gukesh Dommaraju
quotes.source: FIDE interview ("Gukesh Dommaraju: 'I just want to enjoy the experience'"), November 10, 2024

quotes.quote: Just enjoy the game; chess is a beautiful game. It has many benefits.
quotes.author: Gukesh Dommaraju
quotes.source: FIDE interview ("Gukesh Dommaraju: 'I just want to enjoy the experience'"), November 10, 2024

quotes.quote: I felt a bit more freedom to push my luck a little bit.
quotes.author: Gukesh Dommaraju
quotes.source: Post-match interview with GM Maurice Ashley after the 2024 World Chess Championship, December 2024

quotes.quote: I don't think it's pressure if you don't make it as pressure. The fact that at least I have a shot is a good thing for me, I can try, so it's good. I don't feel the pressure.
quotes.author: Alireza Firouzja
quotes.source: Chess.com interview ("Alireza Firouzja: 'I am thinking about improving and having fun'"), June 23, 2023

quotes.quote: I like it a lot. You can't train it, you just have to play it by feeling.
quotes.author: Alireza Firouzja
quotes.source: Chess.com interview ("Alireza Firouzja: 'I am thinking about improving and having fun'"), June 23, 2023

quotes.quote: Everybody knows that it is harder for me to play against Hikaru in rapid and blitz than Magnus.
quotes.author: Alireza Firouzja
quotes.source: Chess.com interview ("Alireza Firouzja: 'I am thinking about improving and having fun'"), June 23, 2023

quotes.quote: For pleasure, peace of mind and the moral torture of their neighbour.
quotes.author: Levon Aronian
quotes.source: Crestbook KC-Conference interview, quoted in Chess.com ("Crestbook interview with Levon Aronian, part 1"), August 31, 2011

quotes.quote: You don't play chess to have fun. You play chess to crush your opponent.
quotes.author: Levon Aronian
quotes.source: Chess.com interview ("Aronian In South Africa: 'Chess Is The Purpose Of My Life'"), January 11, 2020

quotes.quote: Every time I'm playing a simul, people say 'this guy is good, this guy is bad, pay attention to this one'—but I actually don't like that. I like the randomness and I like the fact that I have to put up an effort.
quotes.author: Levon Aronian
quotes.source: Chess.com interview ("Aronian In South Africa: 'Chess Is The Purpose Of My Life'"), January 11, 2020

quotes.quote: I have often been asked, what made me think seriously about chess? It would appear that the atmosphere of silence and heavy smoking is not appropriate for a young lady...
quotes.author: Vera Menchik
quotes.source: Letter/recollection published in CHESS magazine, May 1943 (quoted in Chess.com's "Vera Menchik: The Real-life Beth Harmon")

quotes.quote: I am very thankful that chess was my sport of choice.
quotes.author: Nona Gaprindashvili
quotes.author_role: first woman awarded the FIDE Grandmaster title
quotes.source: ChessBase interview at the 2018 World Senior Championships, Bled

quotes.quote: Yes, I am Nona Gaprindashvili, I am Georgian. Yes, throughout my career I played against male chess players and often defeated them.
quotes.author: Nona Gaprindashvili
quotes.author_role: first woman awarded the FIDE Grandmaster title
quotes.source: Georgia Today interview, January 28, 2022 (statement on her Netflix/Queen's Gambit defamation suit)

quotes.quote: I was honored to become the first female grandmaster among men.
quotes.author: Nona Gaprindashvili
quotes.author_role: first woman awarded the FIDE Grandmaster title
quotes.source: Georgia Today interview, January 2022

quotes.quote: The fight continues until the final victory.
quotes.author: Nona Gaprindashvili
quotes.author_role: first woman awarded the FIDE Grandmaster title
quotes.source: Georgia Today interview, January 28, 2022, on her lawsuit against Netflix over The Queen's Gambit

quotes.quote: The most terrible thing is preparation before the game.
quotes.author: Maia Chiburdanidze
quotes.source: Interview by Evgeny Surov, republished on Chess.com ("Maya Chiburdanidze proposes a new tournament system")

quotes.quote: I think that forcing your opponent to play your limited repertoire is unfair.
quotes.author: Maia Chiburdanidze
quotes.source: Interview by Evgeny Surov, republished on Chess.com

quotes.quote: You should know chess, not learn a lot of computer variants by heart.
quotes.author: Maia Chiburdanidze
quotes.source: Interview by Evgeny Surov, republished on Chess.com

quotes.quote: I grew up in an era when there were very few women playing chess and I had to overcome a lot of challenges just to play in open tournaments with men.
quotes.author: Susan Polgar
quotes.author_role: first woman to earn the full Grandmaster title by norms and rating
quotes.source: Interview reprinted courtesy of Northwest Chess Magazine, Chess.com blog

quotes.quote: Chess trains young people to make good choices in the game of life.
quotes.author: Susan Polgar
quotes.author_role: first woman to earn the full Grandmaster title by norms and rating
quotes.source: Interview reprinted courtesy of Northwest Chess Magazine, Chess.com blog

quotes.quote: I am most proud of breaking the gender barrier, of becoming the first woman in history to earn the 'men's' grandmaster title by norms and rating.
quotes.author: Susan Polgar
quotes.author_role: first woman to earn the full Grandmaster title by norms and rating
quotes.source: USCF Sales interview on her memoir "Rebel Queen"

quotes.quote: While things have improved, unfortunately girls in chess today still face sexist attitudes from some men.
quotes.author: Susan Polgar
quotes.author_role: first woman to earn the full Grandmaster title by norms and rating
quotes.source: USCF Sales interview on her memoir "Rebel Queen"

quotes.quote: They may delay my progress, but they CANNOT stop me.
quotes.author: Susan Polgar
quotes.author_role: first woman to earn the full Grandmaster title by norms and rating
quotes.source: USCF Sales interview on her memoir "Rebel Queen"

quotes.quote: I always felt I had to prove my ability many more times than a boy would have.
quotes.author: Judit Polgar
quotes.author_role: strongest female chess player in history, only woman to break into the world top 10
quotes.source: Chess.com interview, "Judit Polgar Interview: 'I Had To Prove Myself More Than A Boy'"

quotes.quote: You can lose against Garry without making a single move...simply because he made such a strong psychological impression.
quotes.author: Judit Polgar
quotes.author_role: strongest female chess player in history, only woman to break into the world top 10
quotes.source: Chess.com interview, "Judit Polgar Interview: 'I Had To Prove Myself More Than A Boy'"

quotes.quote: Chess is a mind sport and I believe there shouldn't be such a big gap between the men and the women.
quotes.author: Judit Polgar
quotes.author_role: strongest female chess player in history, only woman to break into the world top 10
quotes.source: Chess.com interview, "Judit Polgar Interview: 'I Had To Prove Myself More Than A Boy'"

quotes.quote: Those negative experiences are actually necessary in order to look for new opportunities, be creative, and renew yourself.
quotes.author: Judit Polgar
quotes.author_role: strongest female chess player in history, only woman to break into the world top 10
quotes.source: Chess.com interview, "Judit Polgar Interview: 'I Had To Prove Myself More Than A Boy'"

quotes.quote: I think he made a big growth in his mindset. And he did appreciate and acknowledge my achievements.
quotes.author: Judit Polgar
quotes.author_role: strongest female chess player in history, only woman to break into the world top 10
quotes.source: Chess.com interview, "Judit Polgar Reflects On Queen Of Chess Success, Kasparov" (referring to Garry Kasparov)

quotes.quote: Chess is a game where you can learn a lot. So I wish that chess becomes part of everyday school material, in a fun and an educational way.
quotes.author: Judit Polgar
quotes.author_role: strongest female chess player in history, only woman to break into the world top 10
quotes.source: Chess.com interview, "Judit Polgar Reflects On Queen Of Chess Success, Kasparov"

quotes.quote: At first chess was just a game, later it became a sport and brought the teacher out of me.
quotes.author: Sofia Polgar
quotes.author_role: International Master, middle of the three Polgar sisters
quotes.source: sofiapolgar.com (artist/author statement)

quotes.quote: To be the best female player has no attraction to me. I've been there for years.
quotes.author: Hou Yifan
quotes.source: ESPN feature, "The exceptional genius of Hou Yifan"

quotes.quote: I want my life to be rich and colorful, not narrow.
quotes.author: Hou Yifan
quotes.source: ESPN feature, "The exceptional genius of Hou Yifan"

quotes.quote: Some people's chess styles match their personality perfectly. For me, it's the opposite: In chess I'm aggressive, but not in real life.
quotes.author: Hou Yifan
quotes.source: ESPN feature, "The exceptional genius of Hou Yifan"

quotes.quote: I won't consider staying in a system with which I completely disagree.
quotes.author: Hou Yifan
quotes.source: ESPN feature, "The exceptional genius of Hou Yifan"

quotes.quote: To me the current Women's World Championship system seems to be unfair. And I believe I'm not the only one who thinks like this.
quotes.author: Hou Yifan
quotes.source: ChessBase interview with Dagobert Kohlmeyer, "Interview with Hou Yifan"

quotes.quote: Chess is a part of my life, but it is not my whole life!
quotes.author: Hou Yifan
quotes.source: GibChess interview, YouTube, "Interview with Hou Yifan"

quotes.quote: Despite the outcome, there cannot be winners in wars.
quotes.author: Alexandra Kosteniuk
quotes.source: Chess.com interview, "Interview: Kosteniuk On Federation Change, 'There Cannot Be Winners In Wars'"

quotes.quote: Chess has a very wrong image. People think it's boring, and only fat men in suits play it, so I break that signal and show them chess is cool.
quotes.author: Alexandra Kosteniuk
quotes.source: Christian Science Monitor, "A chess champion crusades to make the game 'cool'"

quotes.quote: You can easily be beautiful and play chess well, or be a professor, or any kind of high achiever.
quotes.author: Alexandra Kosteniuk
quotes.source: Christian Science Monitor, "A chess champion crusades to make the game 'cool'"

quotes.quote: I am not a full-time chess player, like I don't practice. Sometimes I don't even see chess for weeks.
quotes.author: Koneru Humpy
quotes.author_role: second woman ever to cross 2600 FIDE rating, multiple-time World Rapid Champion
quotes.source: Chess.com interview, "Interview With Koneru Humpy On 2nd World Rapid Title, Indian 'Golden Era' & Tips For Improvers"

quotes.quote: It's important for me that I enjoy the game more than the results.
quotes.author: Koneru Humpy
quotes.author_role: second woman ever to cross 2600 FIDE rating, multiple-time World Rapid Champion
quotes.source: Chess.com interview, "Interview With Koneru Humpy On 2nd World Rapid Title, Indian 'Golden Era' & Tips For Improvers"

quotes.quote: I would suggest them to play a lot of men's tournaments...when you have a tough competition, you would automatically rise to the occasion.
quotes.author: Koneru Humpy
quotes.author_role: second woman ever to cross 2600 FIDE rating, multiple-time World Rapid Champion
quotes.source: Chess.com interview, "Interview With Koneru Humpy On 2nd World Rapid Title, Indian 'Golden Era' & Tips For Improvers"

quotes.quote: It's better not to think about the result...once you start the game probably you should erase everything from your mind.
quotes.author: Koneru Humpy
quotes.author_role: second woman ever to cross 2600 FIDE rating, multiple-time World Rapid Champion
quotes.source: Chess.com interview, "Interview With Koneru Humpy On 2nd World Rapid Title, Indian 'Golden Era' & Tips For Improvers"

quotes.quote: Playing chess makes me happier than doing anything else.
quotes.author: Ju Wenjun
quotes.source: ChessBase interview, "Playing chess makes me happier than doing anything else"

quotes.quote: I have maybe a more solid style, positional style, which means I usually feel no need to be very aggressive.
quotes.author: Ju Wenjun
quotes.source: Chess.com interview, "Interview: Ju Wenjun - Women's World Chess Champion 2025"

quotes.quote: I feel very excited. Like, all the stress, when I become champion, when I win a match, all the stress is gone.
quotes.author: Ju Wenjun
quotes.source: Chess.com interview, "Interview: Ju Wenjun - Women's World Chess Champion 2025"

quotes.quote: The game of Chess is not merely an idle amusement; several very valuable qualities of the mind, useful in the course of human life, are to be acquired and strengthened by it, so as to become habits ready on all occasions.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.source: "The Morals of Chess" (essay)

quotes.quote: Life is a kind of chess, in which we have often points to gain, and competitors or adversaries to contend with, and in which there is a vast variety of good and ill events, that are, in some degree, the effect of prudence or the want of it.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.source: "The Morals of Chess" (essay)

quotes.quote: We learn by chess the habit of not being discouraged by present bad appearances in the state of our affairs, the habit of hoping for a favorable change, and that of persevering in the search of resources.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.source: "The Morals of Chess" (essay)

quotes.quote: The passion for playing chess is one of the most unaccountable in the world. It slaps the theory of natural selection in the face.
quotes.author: H.G. Wells
quotes.source: "Concerning Chess," essay in Certain Personal Matters

quotes.quote: There is no remorse like the remorse of chess.
quotes.author: H.G. Wells
quotes.source: "Concerning Chess," essay in Certain Personal Matters

quotes.quote: You have, let us say, a promising politician, a rising artist, that you wish to destroy. Dagger or bomb are archaic, clumsy, and unreliable -- but teach him, inoculate him with chess!
quotes.author: H.G. Wells
quotes.source: "Concerning Chess," essay in Certain Personal Matters

quotes.quote: While all artists are not chess players, all chess players are artists.
quotes.author: Marcel Duchamp
quotes.source: Address at a banquet of the New York State Chess Association, quoted in Arturo Schwarz, The Complete Works of Marcel Duchamp

quotes.quote: Why isn't my chess playing an art activity? A chess game is very plastic. You construct it. It's mechanical sculpture and with chess one creates beautiful problems and that beauty is made with the head and hands.
quotes.author: Marcel Duchamp
quotes.source: Quoted by Truman Capote in Observations (with Richard Avedon)

quotes.quote: Competition in chess problems is not really between White and Black but between the composer and the hypothetical solver (just as in a first-rate work of fiction the real clash is between the author and the world), so that a great part of a problem's value is due to the number of 'tries' -- delusive opening moves, false scents, specious lines of play, astutely and lovingly prepared to lead the would-be solver astray.
quotes.author: Vladimir Nabokov
quotes.source: Speak, Memory (autobiography)

quotes.quote: Chess problems demand from the composer the same virtues that characterize all worthwhile art: originality, invention, conciseness, harmony, complexity, and splendid insincerity.
quotes.author: Vladimir Nabokov
quotes.source: Poems and Problems

quotes.quote: Among a great many other things that chess teaches you is to control the initial excitement you feel when you see something that looks good. It trains you to think before grabbing, and to think just as objectively when you're in trouble.
quotes.author: Stanley Kubrick
quotes.source: Interview with Eric Norden, Playboy magazine

quotes.quote: A good chess player who has lost a game is genuinely convinced that his failure resulted from a false move on his part, and tries to see the mistake he made at the beginning of the game, forgetting that at each stage of play there were similar blunders, so that no single move was perfect.
quotes.author: Leo Tolstoy
quotes.source: War and Peace

quotes.quote: War is like a game of chess ... but with this little difference, that in chess you may think over each move as long as you please and are not limited for time.
quotes.author: Leo Tolstoy
quotes.source: War and Peace

quotes.quote: Les échecs, où l'on ne joue rien, sont le seul jeu qui m'amuse. (Chess, where one plays for nothing, is the only game that amuses me.)
quotes.author: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
quotes.source: Letter to M. de Saint-Germain, 26 February 1770

quotes.quote: The most suitable simile would be that of a game of chess, where the plan we determined to follow is conditioned by the play of our rival -- in life, by the caprice of fate ... we are compelled to modify our tactics, often to such an extent that, as we carry them out, hardly a single feature of the original plan can be recognized.
quotes.author: Arthur Schopenhauer
quotes.source: Counsels and Maxims (Parerga und Paralipomena), trans. T. Bailey Saunders

quotes.quote: A great chess-player is not a great man, for he leaves the world as he found it.
quotes.author: William Hazlitt
quotes.source: Table-Talk

quotes.quote: Life's too short for chess.
quotes.author: Henry James Byron
quotes.source: Our Boys (play), Act I

quotes.quote: Suppose that physics, or rather nature, is considered analogous to a great chess game with millions of pieces in it, and we are trying to discover the laws by which the pieces move ... We do not know what the rules of the game are; all we are allowed to do is to watch the playing.
quotes.author: Richard Feynman
quotes.source: The Character of Physical Law (based on the 1964 Messenger Lectures at Cornell)

quotes.quote: I am explaining chess to someone; and I begin by pointing to a chessman and saying: 'This is the king; it can move like this, ...' -- In this case we shall say: the words 'This is the king' are a definition only if the learner already 'knows what a piece in a game is.'
quotes.author: Ludwig Wittgenstein
quotes.source: Philosophical Investigations, §31

quotes.quote: As elaborate a waste of human intelligence as you could find anywhere outside an advertising agency.
quotes.author: Raymond Chandler
quotes.source: The Long Goodbye (novel, narrated in the voice of detective Philip Marlowe)

quotes.quote: God moves the player, and he, the piece. What God beyond God begins the round of dust and time and sleep and agonies?
quotes.author: Jorge Luis Borges
quotes.source: "Ajedrez" ("Chess"), poem in El Hacedor

quotes.quote: Is the despatch of this chessboard an affair of state? Does this man fear that I shall give check to all the kings of Europe?
quotes.author: Napoleon Bonaparte
quotes.source: Remark to General Bertrand during exile on St Helena, recorded in 19th-century Napoleonic memoirs

quotes.quote: It's a great huge game of chess that's being played -- all over the world -- if this is the world at all, you know. Oh, what fun it is! How I wish I was one of them! I wouldn't mind being a Pawn, if only I might join -- though of course I should like to be a Queen, best.
quotes.author: Lewis Carroll
quotes.source: Through the Looking-Glass, and What Alice Found There

quotes.quote: I am not a chess expert and therefore not in a position to marvel at the force of mind revealed in his greatest intellectual achievement -- in the field of chess.
quotes.author: Albert Einstein
quotes.source: Foreword to J. Hannak, Emanuel Lasker: The Life of a Chess Master

quotes.quote: Anyone who hopes to learn the noble game of chess from books will soon discover that only the openings and end-games admit of an exhaustive systematic presentation and that the infinite variety of moves which develop after the opening defy any such description. The rules which can be laid down for the practice of psycho-analytic treatment are subject to similar limitations.
quotes.author: Sigmund Freud
quotes.author_role: Austrian neurologist and founder of psychoanalysis
quotes.source: "On Beginning the Treatment" (technique paper)

trivia.fact: Wilhelm Steinitz defeated Johannes Zukertort 10 wins to 5 (with 5 draws) in 1886, in the match generally recognized as the first official World Chess Championship.
Wilhelm Steinitz was 50 years old (born May 14, 1836) when he won the first official World Chess Championship in 1886.

Emanuel Lasker took the World Chess Championship from Steinitz in 1894 (score: 10 wins, 5 losses, 4 draws) and held the title for 27 years, from 1894 to 1921 — the longest reign of any recognized World Chess Champion.
Jose Raul Capablanca became the third World Chess Champion in 1921 by defeating Emanuel Lasker.
Alexander Alekhine defeated Capablanca in Buenos Aires in 1927 by a score of +6 −3 =25 over 34 games — the longest World Championship match ever to reach a decisive result.
Max Euwe upset reigning champion Alekhine to win the World Chess Championship in 1935, winning 15.5–14.5.
Alekhine regained the World Chess Championship from Euwe in a 1937 rematch, winning 15.5–9.5.
Alexander Alekhine died in Estoril, Portugal on March 24, 1946, while still reigning World Chess Champion — the only World Chess Champion to die while holding the title.
Mikhail Botvinnik won the 1948 World Chess Championship tournament (held to fill the title left vacant by Alekhine's death) to become the sixth World Champion.

Mikhail Botvinnik held the World Chess Championship across three separate reigns (1948–57, 1958–60, 1961–63), repeatedly winning back the title via a rematch clause that let a deposed champion challenge again immediately.
Vasily Smyslov beat Botvinnik 12.5–9.5 in 1957 to become the seventh World Champion, then lost the title back to Botvinnik 12.5–10.5 in the 1958 rematch.
Mikhail Tal defeated Botvinnik 12.5–8.5 in 1960 to become World Champion at age 23, the youngest champion up to that time; Botvinnik won the title back 13–8 in their 1961 rematch.
Tigran Petrosian defeated Botvinnik 12.5–9.5 in 1963 to become the ninth World Chess Champion, ending Botvinnik's ability to invoke a rematch clause (which FIDE abolished after 1963).
Boris Spassky lost to Petrosian in a 1966 title defense (Petrosian won 12.5–11.5) but defeated Petrosian 12.5–10.5 in their rematch in 1969 to become the tenth World Chess Champion.
Bobby Fischer defeated Boris Spassky 12.5–8.5 in the 1972 Reykjavik match to become the 11th World Chess Champion — the first, and to date only, American to hold the undisputed world title.

Bobby Fischer forfeited the World Chess Championship without playing a game in 1975 after a dispute with FIDE over match conditions — the first forfeited World Championship in history; Anatoly Karpov was declared champion by default on April 3, 1975.
Anatoly Karpov defended his title against Viktor Korchnoi in Baguio, Philippines in 1978, winning 6 wins to 5 with 21 draws over 32 games.
Karpov defended his title against Korchnoi again in Merano, Italy in 1981, winning 6 wins to 2 losses.
trivia.source: Wikipedia: World Chess Championship 1981 (via chess.com summary)

trivia.fact: The 1984–85 Karpov–Kasparov World Championship match was terminated without a result after 48 games (Karpov leading 5 wins to 3, with 40 draws) by FIDE president Florencio Campomanes — the only World Championship match in history to be abandoned without a decision, and the longest world title match ever played by number of games.

Garry Kasparov won the replayed 1985 World Chess Championship match 13–11, becoming champion at age 22 (22 years, 7 months) — the youngest undisputed World Chess Champion at that time, a record that stood until 2024.

Kasparov and Karpov contested five World Chess Championship matches in total between 1984 and 1990 (1984–85, 1985, 1986, 1987, 1990), totaling 144 games — more world title matches than any other pair of opponents in chess history.
In the 1987 Kasparov–Karpov World Championship match in Seville, the score finished tied 12–12; under the rules, a tied match meant the reigning champion (Kasparov) retained the title.
Kasparov won the 1990 rematch against Karpov by a score of 12.5–11.5, his fourth consecutive world title defense against Karpov.

In 1993, Garry Kasparov and challenger Nigel Short broke away from FIDE to form the Professional Chess Association (PCA); Kasparov beat Short 12.5–7.5 for the PCA/'Classical' world title, while FIDE stripped Kasparov of its title and staged a separate Karpov–Timman match (won by Karpov) for the FIDE title — beginning a split of the World Chess Championship that lasted 13 years.
trivia.source: Wikipedia: World Chess Championship 1993 / Professional Chess Association

trivia.fact: FIDE ran its World Chess Championship as a knockout tournament from 1998 to 2004, producing a different champion almost every cycle: Anatoly Karpov (1998), Alexander Khalifman (1999), Viswanathan Anand (2000), Ruslan Ponomariov (2002), and Rustam Kasimdzhanov (2004).

Vladimir Kramnik defeated Garry Kasparov 8.5–6.5 in the 2000 Classical World Chess Championship in London, winning two games and drawing the rest — Kasparov failed to win a single game in the match, a first in his career.

The 2006 World Chess Championship between Vladimir Kramnik and Veselin Topalov in Elista, Russia, reunified the split Classical and FIDE titles after 13 years apart; the classical portion finished tied 6–6, and Kramnik won a rapid tiebreak 2.5–1.5 for an overall match score of 8.5–7.5.

The 2006 Kramnik–Topalov match was marked by the 'Toiletgate' controversy, in which Topalov's team accused Kramnik of receiving illicit computer assistance during bathroom breaks; Kramnik forfeited Game 5 in protest before the match resumed.

Viswanathan Anand won the World Chess Championship in three different formats over his career — knockout (2000), tournament (2007), and match play (2008, 2010, 2012) — the only player to have won the world title under all three formats.
trivia.source: ESPN: How Viswanathan Anand won his five world chess championship titles

trivia.fact: Viswanathan Anand is a five-time World Chess Champion, holding the title in 2000, 2007, 2008, 2010, and 2012, defending it against Kramnik (2008), Topalov (2010), and Gelfand (2012).

Magnus Carlsen defeated Anand 6.5–3.5 (after 10 of 12 scheduled games) in the 2013 World Chess Championship in Chennai, India, becoming champion at age 22 years and 357 days — at the time the second-youngest champion ever, behind Kasparov's 22 years, 210 days.

In July 2022, Magnus Carlsen announced he would not defend his World Chess Championship title in 2023, citing lack of motivation — the first champion to voluntarily relinquish the world title since Bobby Fischer in 1975.
trivia.source: NPR: World chess champion Magnus Carlsen says he will not defend his title in 2023

trivia.fact: Ding Liren defeated Ian Nepomniachtchi in the 2023 World Chess Championship — the 14-game classical match finished tied 7–7, and Ding won the rapid tiebreak 2.5–1.5 — becoming the first World Chess Champion from China.

Gukesh Dommaraju defeated Ding Liren 7.5–6.5 in the 2024 World Chess Championship in Singapore to become, at age 18 years and 197 days, the youngest undisputed World Chess Champion in history, surpassing Kasparov's 1985 record.
trivia.source: Guinness World Records: Youngest Chess World Champion (male)

trivia.fact: The 1910 World Chess Championship match between champion Emanuel Lasker and challenger Carl Schlechter ended level, with Lasker retaining his title; Schlechter needed only a draw in the final game to win the match outright but instead played for a win and lost, one of the closest results in title-match history.
FIDE established the Women's World Chess Championship in 1927; Vera Menchik won the inaugural event with 10 wins and 1 draw in 11 games to become the first Women's World Chess Champion at age 21.

Vera Menchik held the Women's World Chess Championship for almost 17 years (1927 until her death in 1944), winning the title a record eight times — the longest reign of any world chess champion, men's or women's.
Vera Menchik was killed on June 26, 1944, along with her mother and sister, when a German V-1 flying bomb destroyed their home in south London during World War II.
Hou Yifan became the youngest-ever Women's World Chess Champion on December 24, 2010, winning the title at age 16 years, 9 months and 28 days by defeating fellow Chinese player Ruan Lufei.
trivia.source: Guinness World Records: Youngest Chess World Champion (Women's)

trivia.fact: Ju Wenjun won the Women's World Chess Championship in May 2018, defeating Tan Zhongyi 5.5–4.5, and has successfully defended the title multiple times since, including in November 2018, 2020, 2023, and 2025.
trivia.source: Wikipedia: Ju Wenjun; Women's World Chess Championship Match 2018

trivia.fact: Judit Polgar reached a peak FIDE rating of 2735 and a world ranking of No. 8 in 2005 — both remain records for a female player — and she is the only woman to date to have qualified for a Candidates tournament (2005), though she never competed for the separate Women's World Championship.

Steinitz's title reign (1886–1894), Lasker's (1894–1921), and Capablanca's (1921–1927) mean the first three officially recognized World Chess Champions together held the title for 41 consecutive years before Alekhine took over in 1927.
The Karpov–Kasparov 1984–85 match, at five months long (September 10, 1984 to February 8, 1985), is the longest World Chess Championship match in duration in history.

Mikhail Botvinnik is the only World Chess Champion to regain the title twice via rematch clauses, losing and reclaiming the crown against two different opponents (Smyslov in 1957–58, and Tal in 1960–61).
The split between the FIDE and Classical/PCA World Chess Championship titles lasted from 1993 to 2006 — 13 years — before being reunified by the Kramnik–Topalov match.
Karpov's ascent to the World Chess Championship in 1975 was unique in that he became champion without ever playing a match against the previous title holder (Fischer), due to Fischer's forfeit.
Alexander Alekhine's two reigns as World Chess Champion (1927–1935 and 1937–1946) were separated by a two-year interregnum in which Max Euwe held the title (1935–1937).

The Ruy Lopez opening is named after the Spanish priest Ruy López de Segura, whose 1561 treatise 'Libro de la invención liberal y arte del juego del ajedrez' analyzed it, even though he did not invent the opening himself.

The Encyclopaedia of Chess Openings (ECO) classification system, dividing all openings into codes A00–E99, originated in 1966 with the inaugural issue of the Yugoslav magazine Chess Informant, published by Šahovski Informator in Belgrade.

The Caro-Kann Defence is named after Englishman Horatio Caro and Austrian Marcus Kann, whose analysis of 1...c6 was published in 1886; Kann had already scored a notable win with it over Jacques Mieses at the 4th German Chess Congress in Hamburg in 1885.

The French Defence takes its name from an 1834 correspondence match between the London Chess Club and the Paris Chess Club, in which Paris player Jacques Chamouillet persuaded his team to adopt 1...e6, and Paris won the match.
trivia.source: chessgames.com, 'London Chess Club vs Paris Chess Club (1834)'

trivia.fact: Although the Sicilian Defence was analyzed as early as 1594 by Giulio Polerio, the English name 'Sicilian Defence' was standardized only in 1813 by master Jacob Henry Sarratt, translating the Italian phrase 'il gioco siciliano' ('the Sicilian game') from an old manuscript.

The Catalan Opening got its name when tournament organizers at Barcelona 1929 asked Savielly Tartakower to create an opening in homage to Catalonia; he debuted it on 30 September 1929 against Joaquín Torres Caravaca.

The Orangutan Opening (1.b4) got its nickname when Savielly Tartakower visited a New York zoo during the 1924 New York tournament, was impressed by an orangutan there, and dedicated his next game (against Géza Maróczy, 21 March 1924) to it.
1.b4 is also known as the Sokolsky Opening because Soviet player Alexei Sokolsky wrote a 1963 monograph on it, 'Debyut 1 b2–b4'.
The Scotch Game gets its name from an 1824–28 correspondence match between the Edinburgh and London chess clubs, in which Edinburgh won the deciding fifth game using 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4.

The Evans Gambit was invented around 1824–1826 by Welsh sea captain William Davies Evans, who reportedly devised it while sailing between Wales and Ireland and introduced it in a famous London game defeating Irish master Alexander McDonnell.

Ernst Grünfeld introduced the Grünfeld Defence into master play at the Bad Pístany tournament in April 1922, then defeated Alexander Alekhine with it in Vienna that November — a loss that impressed Alekhine enough to try the opening himself in the same event, where he lost with it in 26 moves.

According to his own 1953 autobiography, Russian master and amateur astronomer Fyodor Dus-Chotimirsky claims to have coined the name 'Dragon Variation' in 1901, comparing Black's kingside pawn structure to the stars of the constellation Draco; the earliest known printed use of the name was found by historian Edward Winter in a 1914 issue of Wiener Schachzeitung.

The 'Immortal Game' between Adolf Anderssen and Lionel Kieseritzky, played in London in 1851, was a casual game outside the official London 1851 tournament; it only acquired its famous nickname in 1855, when Austrian player Ernst Falkbeer dubbed it 'The Immortal Game'.

Frank Marshall debuted the Marshall Attack against José Raúl Capablanca on 23 October 1918 in New York; although long believed to have been secretly prepared since 1909, chess historian Edward Winter found the same pawn sacrifice played in a game as far back as 1893.

The Berlin Defence's drawish, solid reputation earned it the nickname 'the Berlin Wall'; it was propelled to modern fame when Vladimir Kramnik used it repeatedly to help dethrone Garry Kasparov in their 2000 World Championship match.

The Berlin Pleiades were a group of seven 19th-century German chess masters (active 1837–1843), named after the star cluster, who included Paul Rudolf von Bilguer and Ludwig Bledow and helped develop early opening theory including the Berlin Defence.

The earliest known game with the Budapest Gambit was a casual game between Mór Adler and Géza Maróczy in Budapest on 5 March 1896, but the opening was only taken seriously after Milan Vidmar, on advice from István Abonyi, used it to defeat Akiba Rubinstein at Berlin in April 1918.

The Benko Gambit was originally called the Volga Gambit in Eastern Europe, after an article on 3...b5 by B. Argunow published in a 1946 issue of the Soviet magazine Shakhmaty v SSSR; the name 'Benko Gambit' took hold in English-speaking countries after Pal Benko's 1974 book on it.

The English Opening (1.c4) is named for Howard Staunton's use of it against Pierre Saint-Amant in their 1843 Paris match, which Staunton won 13–8 and which cemented his status as the world's strongest player.

Petrov's Defence is also called the Russian Game in honor of Alexander Petrov, who extensively analyzed 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 together with fellow Russian Carl Jaenisch and published his findings in his 1824 book 'Shakhmatnaya Igra'.
Aron Nimzowitsch conceived the core idea of the Nimzo-Indian Defence around 1913, but it first appeared at World Championship level only in game two of the 1929 Alekhine–Bogoljubov match.

Bird's Opening (1.f4) had appeared in Luis Ramírez de Lucena's chess book around 1497, but it was English accountant Henry Bird who popularized it from 1855 over a career of more than four decades; the Hereford Times formally named the opening in his honor in 1885.
Alexander Alekhine introduced what became known as Alekhine's Defence (1.e4 Nf6) at the Budapest tournament of 1921, playing it in games against Endre Steiner and Friedrich Sämisch.

François-André Danican Philidor introduced 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 d6 — now called the Philidor Defence — in his own 1749 book 'Analyse du jeu des Échecs', in which he coined the maxim 'pawns are the soul of chess'.
trivia.source: chesshistory.com (Edward Winter), 'Philidor: Pawns are the soul of chess'

trivia.fact: The classic queen-sacrifice trap known as Legal's Mate is named after the 18th-century French player Sire de Legall, drawn from a game he supposedly played (at rook odds) against an opponent named Saint Brie in Paris around 1750; historians note the exact date and move order of the original game are disputed.

The Fried Liver Attack takes its name from 'fegatello,' an Italian dish of roasted or pan-fried pig's liver — a metaphor for Black's king being 'cooked' in White's mating net; the line is also called the Fegatello Attack and dates back to at least the 17th century.

The 'Opera Game' — Paul Morphy's famous 1858 miniature against the consulting pair Duke Karl of Brunswick and Count Isouard — was played in a box at the Salle Le Peletier in Paris while an opera (likely Rossini's 'The Barber of Seville', per research by Edward Winter) was being performed on stage.
trivia.source: chesshistory.com (Edward Winter), 'Morphy v the Duke and Count'

trivia.fact: The Traxler Counterattack in the Two Knights Defence first appeared in the game J. Reinisch–Karel Traxler, played in Hostouň in 1890; it is also called the Wilkes-Barre Variation in the US and UK after Frank Marshall, who claimed to have independently analyzed and published the line, named it for the Pennsylvania town.
